newsitem.title: USA: ATLANTA FED ECONOMIST SEES RISE IN MANUFACTURING.
newsitem.headline: ATLANTA FED ECONOMIST SEES RISE IN MANUFACTURING.

text.p: The manufacturing sector in the U.S. Southeast is picking up some mild momentum, a rise accompanied by some uptick in prices, Mark Rogers, a senior economist at the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta said on Tuesday.
"There is a continuation of a mild pick-up in terms of momentum. It's not dramatic," Mark Rogers said in an interview with Reuters Financial Television (RFTV).

"Clearly the new orders, the backlog, the shipments, the employment data are suggesting the Southeastern manufacturing economy is strengthening somewhat," Rogers said, referring to the July survey put out by the Atlanta Fed on Tuesday.
The Atlanta Fed reported earlier on Tuesday that its index of industry business activity surged to 23.3 in July from a revised 15.3 in June.

Several components of the index recorded sharp gains in July versus June: prices received stood at 10.9 vs. zero, new orders 20.1 vs. 10.8, shipments 26.7 vs. 14.8, the number of employees 9.6 vs. 5.8.

"Clearly, we did have a meaningful increase in the prices received index," Rogers acknowledged while stressing however, that the increases seemed "concentrated in the food industry," meaning there was no concern yet about broad-based inflation.

"The price numbers have been on a mild upward trend since earlier in the year," Rogers said. "We have seen a bottoming out in terms of weak price numbers and now we may have seen a mild rise in price pressures, perhaps leveling off."

The July spike in the Atlanta Fed's price received component coincided with an actual decline in prices paid -- a hint that manufacturers may be confident enough in consumer demand to try and improve profit margins by raising prices.
But Rogers noted it was too early to draw such inference from the July price data which may have been distorted by seasonal factors.
